messages:
ana: quick heads-up — I found an edge case in snapshot restores related to CMK rotation. Some DB snapshots created before our automated CMK rotation now fail to restore because the restore service principal doesn't have permissions on the old CMK. :eyes:

mike: which snapshots/bucket? example key?

ana: bucket: redwood-prod-backups, prefix: db-snapshots/2025-*/manifest.json. Example object: db-snapshots/2025-04-02/postgres-001/snapshot-manifest.json. Error seen in restore job: `AccessDenied: arn:aws:kms:...:key/OLD-CMK cannot be used to decrypt`

samir: ok — two axes here: RBAC for restore flow, and audit trail for who/what used the old key. We need CloudTrail KMS events + S3 object-level ops forwarded to SIEM. Retention needs to match compliance (3y for customers with regs).

rachel: also flagging vuln triage: backup-agent v1.4.2 is flagged with CVE-2026-1234 (metadata parsing overflow). We need to decide if we pause restores until we confirm snapshots are not poisoned. Does the CVE allow arbitrary metadata injection on snapshot manifests?

ana: initial triage: CVE affects malformed manifest parsing in the agent that reads snapshot metadata during restore. It could cause daemon crash but no memory corruption in our test harness. Still, precautionary: block automated restores from snapshots produced by agents < "1.4.3", and require manual approval.

ops-oncall: adding runbook snippet for emergency key access change (from ops playbook):

```
# emergency: allow restore role to use archived key
{
  "Sid": "AllowRestoreOnArchivedKey",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restore-service"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringEquals": {"kms:ViaService": "s3.amazonaws.com"}
  }
}
```

ops-oncall: note: prefer key policy change + explicit audit alert. This should be timeboxed (15m) and reverted. :lock:

mike: can we instead grant a short-lived KMS grant rather than changing key policy? grants are auditable too and easier to revoke.

ana: good point. grants are preferred for short-lived access. But our KMS rotation process currently archives the old key and removes grants. We need a small exception path: infra can issue a grant scoped to the restore decrypt operation with a tag/evidence id.

kms-bot: KMS grant creation request logged: request_id=kr-7890 by infra-deploy at 1772500200 — awaiting approval.

rachel: for compliance customers we have to include provenance in the snapshot metadata (creator id, agent version, producing key id). If we don't have that, we'll need to reconstruct from CloudTrail and object ETags which is messy. We should require adding those fields to the manifest schema.

samir: I'll own audit aggregation — plan: enable CloudTrail event selectors for kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:CreateGrant, and S3:GetObject on the backups bucket; forward to splunk index:sec_backups. Also add an alert: any kms:CreateGrant for backup keys triggers high-priority pager duty if created outside infra service account.

mike: also add an alert for key policy changes (PutKeyPolicy) and for kms:DisableKey rotation events.

ana: for the immediate mitigation I propose:
- block automatic restores from snapshots whose manifest.agent_version < "1.4.3"
- issue a time-limited KMS grant to restore-service for archived key with audit tag `inc=1772500000`
- run integrity check on 10 random snapshots from affected date range
- open incident ticket and notify affected customers if evidence of tampering

rachel: +1. Also schedule key rotation verification run for all DB backup keys and generate a provenance report for compliance customers.

ops-oncall: created incident INC-2026-0452 and added playbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backup-key-incident. Ops will perform grant issuance and revert at 1772500300 UTC unless told otherwise.

samir: aws cli commands I will run to wire up CloudTrail selectors / splunk:
```
aws cloudtrail put-event-selectors --trail-name redwood-trail --event-selectors '[{"ReadWriteType":"All","IncludeManagementEvents":true,"DataResources":[{"Type":"AWS::S3::Object","Values":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-backups/"]},{"Type":"AWS::KMS::Key","Values":["arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/"]}]}]'
```

samir: will also create splunk forwarder rule and dashboards for Decrypt/Grant/CreateGrant trends.

mike: one more ops detail — when you create a KMS grant include `GrantConstraints` to limit encryption context to `aws:s3:object-prefix` so the grant can't be reused for other objects.

ana: noted. assigning owners: samir => audit infra + splunk; ops-oncall => temporary grant + revert; rachel => compliance prov report + customer comms; mike => update RBAC doc for restore-service; ana => coordinate and post status to #incidents. I'll follow up with a short postmortem template after we close the loop. :thumbsup:

kms-bot: KMS grant kr-7890 created by infra-deploy at 1772500255.

ana: thanks all. please add any missing blockers here. If we get any failed restores after the grant is revoked, we escalate to on-call infra.

mike: adding quick note for future: include `producing_key_id` and `agent_version` in manifest schema v2.0 before next rollout.

rachel: FYI legal asked to retain all audit logs as-is until the investigation is closed.

ana: ack. closing thread after ops confirms revert.
